recent_posts.title: Reflections on My Tech Career – Part 2
recent_posts.summary: A veteran software developer shares the second half of his career journey, spanning roles at Cavedog/Humongous Entertainment, Microsoft (Xbox 360), Valve, and Google. He specialized in debugging, performance optimization, and fixing critical bugs rather than building features. Notable achievements include discovering CPU design bugs, creating profiling tools, optimizing game performance, and investigating quadratic algorithms. The narrative covers compensation negotiation strategies, the importance of interviewing regularly, and lessons about work-life balance before retiring in 2024.

recent_posts.title: Reflections on My Tech Career – Part 1
recent_posts.summary: A software developer shares the first half of their 37-year career journey, from dropping out of university in the 1980s to landing their first programming jobs. The story covers self-teaching assembly language and C on Amiga computers, creating successful shareware products like MandFXP and CygnusEd, and working at game studios and software companies. Key themes include the importance of performance estimation, side projects as career accelerators, and balancing work with life experiences like a two-year world travel break.

recent_posts.title: Finding a VS Code Memory Leak
recent_posts.summary: A developer discovered a 64 GB memory leak in VS Code by noticing seven-digit process IDs during a pair-programming session, indicating a process handle leak. The investigation revealed that OpenProcess calls lacked corresponding CloseProcess calls, causing roughly 64 KiB of memory to leak per unclosed handle. Using Windows handle leak debugging techniques and tools, the root cause was identified within an hour—a single missing line of code in the process memory usage function. The bug was reported and fixed within days.

recent_posts.title: Acronis True Image Costs Performance When Not Used
recent_posts.summary: The installation of Acronis True Image, even when not actively used, can cause excessive CPU usage by Explorer.exe due to frequent calls to system functions intended for process enumeration. This leads to noticeable performance degradation, especially during USB monitor plug/unplug actions. Acronis acknowledges the issue and plans a fix, while users can mitigate the problem by uninstalling the software or removing specific registry entries.

recent_posts.title: Google Maps' address mapping flaws uncovered
recent_posts.summary: Google Maps has been found to inaccurately map certain street addresses, leading to people being directed to incorrect locations. Errors such as directing users to addresses that don't exist or placing addresses far from their actual locations suggest that Google Maps may not fully understand how street addresses work. These mistakes have real-world consequences, as evidenced by actors arriving late for auditions. The author notes that while some fixes have been implemented, many errors remain uncorrected.

recent_posts.title: What this blog is about
recent_posts.summary: The Random ASCII blog discusses various technical issues and solutions encountered by the author, Bruce Dawson. These include investigative bug fixes in Windows, performance problems with Chrome, and quirky personal stories. Notable posts feature solutions to desktop icon rearrangement bugs, Chrome hang issues, and accurate floating-point number comparisons.

recent_posts.title: Find me on bsky
recent_posts.summary: The author has transitioned from a popular microblogging platform due to concerns about disinformation to using bsky. They invite readers to follow them on bsky for various posts about tech debates, transportation, housing, tech failures, vacation photos, and astronomy.

recent_posts.title: Life, death, and retirement
recent_posts.summary: The author shares a deeply personal account of the events following the sudden illness and eventual death of his wife from pancreatitis. The grief and lack of social support led him to find remote work unhelpful in the healing process. After trying reduced work hours and eventually a leave of absence, he found that he did not miss work. With the approval of his financial adviser, he decided to retire, focusing on life over work. He also mentions being open to future blog posts and private consulting for those with Windows performance issues.

recent_posts.title: Localization Failure: Temperature is Hard
recent_posts.summary: A headline misleads readers by wrongly converting 20 degrees Celsius to 68 degrees Fahrenheit due to a localization error. The correct conversion should be 36 degrees Fahrenheit or -4 degrees Fahrenheit.

recent_posts.title: 32 MiB Working Sets on a 64 GiB machine
recent_posts.summary: The article discusses the issue of limiting the working set of a process on Windows machines. It explains how this feature works, the impact on performance, and the lack of memory-saving benefits. The author also shares their investigation into performance problems with Chrome's setup.exe and suggests potential resolutions.
